uzbekistan.overview: Uzbekistan's best walking lies away from its famous Silk Road cities, up in the Western Tian Shan and the Nuratau mountains. Day hikers head to the Chimgan area near Tashkent, where routes range from the loop over Little Chimgan to the steep, rocky ascent of Greater Chimgan. The scenery shifts from arid foothills to alpine meadows and rugged ridges. Spring and fall offer the best weather for the lower ranges.

months.5: The loop on Little Chimgan opens up with green alpine meadows, offering some of the year's best hiking conditions.

vancouver-island.overview: Vancouver Island is defined by its rugged Pacific coastline and dense temperate rainforests. The main route is the West Coast Trail, a demanding 47-mile, six-to-eight-day trek through deep mud, wooden ladders, and remote beaches that requires advance permits. Day hikers can explore shorter boardwalks and coastal paths in Pacific Rim National Park, passing giant cedars and tidal pools.

months.9: Early autumn brings a return of regular rain, but the West Coast Trail remains open through the end of the month. The rainforest takes on a misty atmosphere.

venice.overview: Venice is a city of canals and pedestrian alleys. Walkers here find flat strolls along the Lido's beaches or the agricultural paths of Sant'Erasmo island; the Dolomites are a separate trip.

months.2: Cold and damp conditions continue, with flat walks on the barrier islands offering chilly outings.

vermont.overview: Vermont offers classic New England hiking through the dense forests of the Green Mountains. The main route is the Long Trail, a rugged 273-mile trek spanning the state, while day hikers tackle the steep, rocky ascents of Mount Mansfield and Camel's Hump for sweeping views over the valleys. Lower elevations provide gentler loops through maple and birch woods.

months.4: Spring thaw creates deep mud, and hikers are asked to stay off the high-elevation trails to protect the fragile alpine zones.
months.5: Lower trails dry out and open for spring hiking, while hikers are asked to avoid high peaks like Mount Mansfield until late in the month to protect the alpine tundra.
months.11: The leaves have fallen and temperatures drop sharply, leaving trails often dusted with early snow.

vienna.overview: Vienna offers accessible day hiking in the Vienna Woods, a forested ridge easily reached by train or tram. Walkers can take on easy trails up Kahlenberg for views over the city and the Danube, or explore the shaded paths of the Hagenbachklamm gorge.

months.2: Late winter keeps the woods chilly and bare, though the lower trails are clear for walking.
months.4: Warmer spring days bring green foliage to the Hagenbachklamm gorge, offering excellent conditions for day hikes.
months.6: Early summer brings warm weather and deep shade on the trails through the Hagenbachklamm gorge.
months.7: Warm days make the shaded forest ridges and the Hagenbachklamm gorge the most comfortable places to walk.
months.8: Summer warmth continues, and the beech-shaded trails of the Vienna Woods stay pleasant even on the hottest afternoons.
months.9: Early fall offers warm days, cooler mornings and clear views from the ridges over the city and the Danube.
months.11: The leaves drop and temperatures fall, leaving the trails brisk for late autumn walks.
months.12: Cold, short days and occasional snow settle on the Vienna Woods, though the lower forest paths stay open for brisk walks.

vietnam.overview: Vietnam's best walking is in the northern highlands, where trails link remote villages through terraced valleys and steep limestone peaks. The main draws are multi-day homestay treks around Sapa and Ha Giang, and the demanding guided climb up Fansipan. The season is driven by the monsoon, with heavy summer rains turning trails to deep mud.

months.11: Crisp, dry weather makes this an ideal month for the demanding guided ascent of Fansipan and long days on the Ha Giang trails.

whistler.overview: Vancouver and Whistler offer mountain hiking, from coastal rainforests to the high alpine of Garibaldi Provincial Park. Day hikers can tackle steep ascents to glacier-fed lakes and panoramic ridges, or explore lower valley loops. The best alpine routes, like the trails to Garibaldi Lake and Joffre Lakes, require free day passes in summer. The high country is strictly a summer destination, with snow burying the peaks for much of the year.

months.2: Snowpack is deep in the mountains, and winter rain soaks the coast. Snowshoe routes and low valley paths are the practical options.
months.3: Snow still blankets the high country while the lowlands turn wet and mild. Valley and coastal forest paths are the main walking.
months.6: Mid-elevation trails open up, though hikers will still find mud and lingering snow patches. The highest alpine routes usually hold snow until late in the month.
